claims.title: Persistent latent-mixture likelihood ratio is a posterior-weighted average of component prior-weight ratios
claims.scope: one latent model drawn once from one of two finite mixing vectors, followed by an arbitrary common model-conditional transcript channel
assumptions: denominator mixing weights are strictly positive
the conditional transcript law given latent model is the same under both mixing-weight hypotheses
nonclaims: the theorem does not constrain evidence about the latent model itself
the result is not evidence for simulation

claims.title: One persistent latent draw imposes transcript-length-independent prior-ratio evidence ceilings
claims.scope: the same finite persistent-latent mixture model
assumptions: the chosen transcript has positive denominator-mixture probability
nonclaims: the ceiling concerns mixing-weight hypotheses rather than transcript distinguishability between component models

claims.title: Mutually singular component transcript laws can attain the persistent prior-ratio evidence ceiling
claims.scope: finite latent mixtures with a transcript event identifying one component exactly
assumptions: the identifying event has positive probability under the selected denominator component
nonclaims: not every overlapping component family attains the bound

claims.title: Evidence about mixing weights multiplies across independent latent draws rather than conditionally repeated observations from one draw
claims.scope: independent units whose latent models are freshly drawn from the same candidate mixing distribution
assumptions: units are independent conditional on their fresh latent draws
nonclaims: within-unit observations may still strongly identify that unit's latent model

claims.title: One hundred noiseless repetitions from one persistent binary model give the same mixing-weight Bayes factor as one repetition
claims.scope: binary persistent latent M with Y_t=M and theta hypotheses 3/4 versus 1/4
assumptions: the same M persists for all repetitions
nonclaims: the corresponding fresh-redraw model has a different likelihood and different evidence scaling

claims.title: Treating persistent binary repetitions as fresh IID latent draws spuriously exponentiates the mixing-weight likelihood ratio
claims.scope: the same binary example comparing persistent and fresh-redraw causal models
assumptions: the IID comparator redraws M independently before each observation
nonclaims: the fresh-redraw model is not called mathematically invalid; it is a different causal hypothesis

claims.title: Bounded exact persistent-latent prior evidence audit
claims.scope: convex-average likelihood-ratio certificates, singular-component saturation, persistent versus IID binary repetition, and independent-unit multiplication
assumptions: all finite probabilities use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded checks are not an empirical validation of any simulation prior
CI success is not evidence for simulation
